assertions.description: BluetoothRemoteGATTServer is exposed on the global object (Web Bluetooth available; on desktop Linux this requires the experimental WebBluetooth runtime flag).
BluetoothRemoteGATTServer.prototype inherits from EventTarget — the IDL change 'interface BluetoothRemoteGATTServer : EventTarget'.
The direct prototype of BluetoothRemoteGATTServer.prototype is exactly EventTarget.prototype (no intermediate interface).
addEventListener is available on the server prototype and is the inherited EventTarget method, not a redefined copy.
dispatchEvent resolves to a function through the server's prototype chain.
The server exposes the onmaxwritewithoutresponsesizechanged event-handler attribute — the first connection-level event this inheritance change enables.
gattserverdisconnected remains a BluetoothDevice event (the spec did not move it to the server): the ongattserverdisconnected handler lives on BluetoothDevice.prototype.
assertions.test: typeof BluetoothDevice !== 'undefined' && 'ongattserverdisconnected' in BluetoothDevice.prototype && (typeof BluetoothRemoteGATTServer === 'undefined' || !('ongattserverdisconnected' in BluetoothRemoteGATTServer.prototype))

assertions.description: On a live GATT connection, connection-level events (e.g. maxwritewithoutresponsesizechanged after MTU renegotiation) dispatch with event.target === the server instance.
assertions.test: Requires real BLE hardware, a user gesture for requestDevice(), and a link whose MTU renegotiates. Use the live-server-events concept page: connect a device and observe the logged 'e.target === server: true' when the event fires.
